_activity: Match the question to its thesis: 11.1
_licence: ORIGINAL, built on the shipped 11.1 casefiles. Quotes are the casefile's own text.
intro: Match each question to the thesis that answers it. A thesis is a claim somebody could argue with.

left.label: Was indentured servitude a fair deal?
How did colonial law build slavery?
What did Native nations lose as the colonies grew?
Why did Franklin want the colonies to unite in 1754?

right.label: Indentured servitude looked fair on paper, but servants like Richard Frethorne paid for it with sickness and hunger.
Colonial law built slavery one statute at a time, turning servants into property by 1705.
As the colonies grew, Native nations lost their land, their game and their food, and leaders like Miantonomo saw it coming.
Colonial self-government was real, but it left out women, who lost their legal identity when they married.
Franklin wanted the colonies to unite because, divided, they could not defend themselves against France.

rationale.a: It takes a side and gives a reason from Document 10.
rationale.b: It answers “how” with a claim about a process, from Document 13.
rationale.c: It names what was lost, using Document 4.
rationale.d: It admits self-government was real, then shows who it left out (Documents 17 and 18).
rationale.e: It answers “why” with a reason, from Document 16.
